title: hierarchical-comm-scheduler-with-layer-aware-kernel-selection-and-kv-prefetch-pipelining
author: Jinwoo Park
description: Motivation: large tensor-parallel workloads continue to see tail-latency and suboptimal bandwidth utilization on multi-socket multi-node clusters when model layer shapes vary. Existing static ring/allreduce placement and uniform chunking interact poorly with KV-cache prefetch windows and per-layer kernel performance characteristics. This PR introduces a hierarchical communication scheduler plus two complementary runtime optimizations: (1) layer-aware kernel selection that picks fused vs unfused kernels per-layer and preempts long-running kernels when small low-latency requests arrive, and (2) a KV-prefetch pipelining manager that overlaps eager shard transfers with compute at per-layer granularity. Summary of changes and goals: implement a two-level communicator partitioning (intra-socket local rings + inter-socket bridges) with adaptive chunk sizing based on recent per-link throughput; introduce a windowed send schedule that staggers chunk launches to avoid head-of-line blocking; add a layer profiler that collects microbenchmarks to choose attention/ffn kernels and a cooperative preemption path to yield GPU SMs for urgent batches; implement a prefetch manager that ties KV cache transfers to layer boundaries, supports speculative fetches for likely next prefixes, and a conservative eviction policy based on per-prefix hit probability. Checklist: - [x] scheduler core, communicator creation and runtime config - [x] adaptive chunking heuristics + runtime telemetry - [x] layer profiler and kernel selector - [x] cooperative preemption path and safe-fallback - [x] KV prefetch manager + eviction heuristics - [x] unit tests and integration perf harness - [x] documentation and runtime flags Design notes: hierarchical scheduler groups ranks by NIC topology to minimize cross-socket hops; per-channel token-bucket backpressure prevents a single large layer from starving others; adaptive chunk size uses an exponentially weighted moving average of recent allreduce bandwidth and latency to pick chunk sizes that maximize throughput while keeping per-chunk latency under the configured SLO. The layer-aware kernel selector stores choices keyed by (layer-id, seq-len, batch-size) and falls back to a cost model when unseen. Cooperative preemption exposes a short-latency interrupt path that runs a small handoff kernel to flush critical outputs and resume preempted work; this is gated behind a runtime flag and tested to avoid deadlocks. KV prefetch manager ties prefetch offsets to the model's layer order and allows speculative prefetch up to N layers ahead with a configurable byte cap; prefetches are demoted if they miss a hit threshold. Performance highlights (internal perf lab, p3dn-24 + 8xA100 config, tensor-parallel 8): - end-to-end throughput +18% on GPT-like 8B eval workload - 95th latency reduced from 340ms to 220ms for mixed short/long queries - KV cache hit-rate improved by 6 percentage points for conversational prefix workloads - network transmission tail reduced by 28% due to staggered chunk launches Testing and CI: included new unit tests for communicator construction, simulated perf harness tests for chunking heuristics, and end-to-end nightly perf job. One flaky test (integration/kv_prefetch_eviction) required two re-runs in CI and was stabilized with an extra timing fence. Deployment notes: runtime flags exposed under redwood.runtime.comm.* and redwood.runtime.kv_prefetch.*. Default rollout is gated behind a canary scoreboard in perf-canary and will be enabled for Dedicated pools after a 2-week canary with perf thresholds. Migration: no API changes; operators can tune chunk_size_policy and prefetch_max_layers. Rollback: feature guarded via runtime flags and can be turned off without model restarts. Files changed and rationale: net/comm/scheduler/hierarchical_scheduler.cc/hpp - core scheduling logic; net/comm/bridge_manager.cc - inter-socket bridge orchestration; runtime/kernel_selector.cpp - layer profiler and kernel selection; runtime/preemption/cooperative_path.cu - safe preemption handoff; runtime/kv_prefetch/manager.cc - prefetch pipeline and eviction; perf/harness/tp_hierarchical_bench.py - integration benchmark; docs/rtd/runtime_comm.md - design and tuning guide; tests/unit/* - new unit tests. Commits: - "proto: hierarchical scheduler initial scaffolding and communicator builder" - "perf: adaptive chunk size heuristics + EWMA bandwidth estimator" - "runtime: layer profiler and kernel selector with persistent cache" - "gpu: cooperative preemption handoff kernel and safety checks" - "kv: prefetch pipeline manager, eviction, and metrics" - "tests: unit and perf harness for TP hierarchical scheduling" Review summary and conversation: Reviewer Ariella Gomez: "Great decomposition; can we quantify additional CPU overhead from the layer profiler?" Author reply: "Profiler uses lightweight timers amortized across warmup steps; added microbenchmark showing ~1.6% CPU overhead on controller & explained in docs." Reviewer Samir Patel: "Concerned about deadlocks in preemption path when combined with persistent streams." Author reply: "Added additional fences and a stress test simulating preemption loops; updated cooperative_path.cu to assert safe state transitions." Reviewer Maya Hopkins (perf): "Adaptive chunking seems to favor smaller chunks on our 40GbE staging clusters; how does policy adapt on 100Gb?" Author reply: "EWMA learns the observed throughput and picks larger chunks on 100Gb links; added a regression test for link-speed emulation." CI summary: build/linux - pass, unit - pass, integration - pass (one flaky kv_prefetch_eviction re-run), perf-nightly - pass (canary report attached). Merge notes: squashed by Jinwoo Park, merge method squash, merge commit message references ENG-3289. Backports/Followups: a follow-up PR will add telemetry dashboards and a runtime knob for cooperative preemption aggressiveness. Release notes: "Introduce hierarchical communication scheduler to improve multi-socket TP bandwidth utilization, layer-aware kernel selection to reduce tail latency, and KV prefetch pipelining to raise effective cache hit rates. Default off for hosted customers; Enabled for Dedicated canaries and opt-in via runtime flags."
